## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (ollaya-f32, needs 8.2 GB, NVIDIA only, from [github.com/ollaya-dev](https://github.com/ollaya-dev/ollaya/blob/9b8698e39f11a0f0bcd08ad686de51cd1b4f6fa8/results/runs/2026-10-24-latency-rtx5090-cuda-d3.json))
   
   ```sh
   ollaya run d3:nano --preset triage "The customer requests a refund."
   ```

[Download model files](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-nano/tree/462efc366229ea268cf4eed3738b3fc4415e4817) · Published model files verified.
